title: Learn-many LDR atoms then Mirror-compose and prune
hypothesis: An overcomplete bank of learned Toeplitz/LDR atoms can be physically pruned after task-code fitting while retaining held-out function quality, using fewer actual bytes than independent Toeplitz kernels; random pruning and small-from-start controls test whether post-training selection matters.
physical_object: overcomplete bank of 32 length-64 Toeplitz atoms, each stored by its first row/column generators
mirror_coordinate: per-task sparse atom IDs and signed floating-point coefficients
logical_multiplicity: 24 task-specific linear maps composed from two atoms each
controls: full 32-atom bank with dense per-task coefficients
ordinary sparse coding over the same atoms
random prune to equal bank size

development.selection_metric: held-out NRMSE, full serialized payload bytes, active compute proxy, atom survival and reconstruction setup cost

success_gate: Across all three audit seeds, post-fit pruned payload retains mean held-out NRMSE <=1e-5, is <=60% of independent Toeplitz payload and <=10% independent dense payload, uses no more than 2x Toeplitz apply proxy including one-time composition amortized over 128 queries, and strictly beats both equal-size random prune and small-from-start on quality at equal bytes. Native ordinary sparse coding exact alias is FAIL for Mirror-specific attribution.
failure_gate: Native sparse coding matches function/bytes/compute, or post-fit pruning does not meet frozen quality/byte/compute gates, or random/small-from-start performs equally well. Report generic sparse LDR feasibility separately.
boundaries: Synthetic linear regression tasks generated as sparse combinations of Toeplitz atoms; this is aligned mechanism screening, not natural task quality or model capacity.
Atom matrices are generated as Toeplitz atoms for controlled identifiability; the experiment does not train a production transform model.
Pruning and coefficient fitting use task support examples only; audit vectors are held out.
No GPU/fused kernel/runtime conclusion; MACs are analytic proxies.
